sampling_model.design: Conditional on each fixed covariate stratum, \(Z\) is randomized with known \(\pi_z(x)=P(Z=z\mid X=x)\) and \(\min_{x,z}\{P(X=x),\pi_z(x)\}\ge\pi_*\); the observed count vector satisfies \(N_n\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}\{n,p_n(u)\}\).
sampling_model.units: The categorical support \(\mathcal J\), rational wage grid \(\mathcal Y\), rational quantile grid \(\mathcal T\), and assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\) are fixed while \(n\to\infty\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument \(Z\), received treatment \(D\), and selection indicator \(S\) are binary; wages are observed only when \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Positive multinomial cells, randomized-instrument support, and target-mass positivity remain distinct conditions. Causal tangent legality additionally requires \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\); both are certified from rational response-type face data.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On every fixed compact, base convergence and the centered local expansion imply eventual positive cells and lawful causal parameters. Carter then contributes only the bounded-ratio experiment error; the score mean, covariance, active-face remainder, rational offset, and semantic-union displacement are charged separately. The diagonal radius records exactly where all such compact moduli have passed, and no premise constrains a label boundary inserted beyond that radius.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.4 proves that recession cones form a rational fan under connectedness and the Minkowski--Weyl condition.
Theorems 3.32 and 4.8 construct a compatible compactified polyhedral complex and compute its Hasse diagram combinatorially.
Corollary 4 gives an explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization error for Gaussian integration over a polytope.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a near-optimal affine detector for two compact convex composite hypotheses through a convex-concave saddle point.
Theorems 1--3 prove convergence of finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations to compact-parameter minimax expected-size confidence regions.
Theorem 1.3 gives a randomized \(O^*(n^3)\) relative-error algorithm for Gaussian volume of a convex set containing the unit ball in the membership-oracle model.
The paper gives convergence conditions for adaptive discretization of finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs with unbounded variables.
Theorem 1 bounds the Le Cam distance between a multinomial experiment and a matching Gaussian experiment when cell-probability ratios are bounded.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform coverage for calibrated projection under drifting moment inequalities, and Theorem 3.2 gives an optimization convergence rate on a compact rectangle.
The paper derives sharp marginal quantile-treatment-effect bounds under truncation by death.
Propositions 1--2 derive nonparametric bounds for average wage effects among always-employed compliers in Job Corps.

Under the complier-conditional weak-selection condition in Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1 gives sharp mean SLATE bounds for always-selected compliers, and Theorem 4.1 gives inference and joint asymptotic normality.

Theorem 1 proves minimum average Lebesgue volume for the inverted minimal-cardinality multinomial covering collections of Definition 1, and Proposition 1 selects a maximum-coverage tie-break among those minimizers.

Section 5 and Proposition 1 present sharp quantile-treatment-effect bounds for the always-employed stratum under random assignment and individual-level employment monotonicity, and Section 6.4 evaluates those bounds at multiple Job Corps wage quantiles.

body.tldr: Finite rational projection active sets now yield computable safe recession sectors preserving every incident semantic label and the separated domain. A barycentric lower-skeleton induction uses literally shared traces, while slow collars control data-dependent chart selection and every weighted-ledger term. This proves effective compatible density with the explicit rational modulus \(A_{\mathfrak G}/j(m)^2+1/j(m)\), so the effective-density premise of CertGluePFL is discharged. Carter-backed multinomial conclusions remain compact or expanding-window conclusions, and the explicit four-label milliscale numerical receipt has not yet been produced.

project_justification.gap: Carter's bounded-ratio theorem does not compare moving causal truth regions or control parameters escaping every compact. For the Gaussian certificate problem, the missing step was simultaneous recession compatibility on a branching incidence poset; commuting one-ray averages alone did not supply it.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification assertions combine completed boundary labels, intersecting unbounded polyhedral ends, and global honesty. The needed compactification must preserve both all incident coverage constraints and the unique-label separated-risk domain, including at branching recession faces.
project_justification.fill: The new construction enumerates projection active sets, stratifies positive-semidefinite recession forms by their kernels, computes safe canonical tail sections, and extends one smoothed ancestor over the barycentric skeleton with exact shared traces. Slow rational collars, guarded Gaussian tails, common-face finite elements, and global full-set repair give the computable modulus and complete ledger required by effective compatible density.

body.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) remains confined to bounded-ratio multinomial laws and their matched Gaussian experiments. Classical invariant-mean and single-action Følner results do not provide a finite modulus or branching semantic compatibility and are not used to close the theorem. The present proof instead uses finite rational projection systems and a new exact shared-trace induction; existing Gaussian-integration and semi-infinite-programming references remain certification components rather than sources of the recession theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The computable safe-sector radii and physical collar widths may grow very rapidly as angular margins shrink, so the proof supplies termination and total recursive certification rather than a practical complexity rate. The explicit four-label outward-rounded gap of \(.001\) remains a numerical artifact to execute and archive. Compact-uniform multinomial assumptions still do not imply a global upper minimax transfer because an assertion boundary may escape every fixed compact.
body.honest_scope: The effective compatible-density claim is now proved for the fully encoded finite union of rational polyhedra with positive rational covariance and nonempty separated domain stated in the experiment class. Its output is a finite rational class and an input-computable, potentially very conservative modulus; it does not claim equality of independent face and cone averages. Gaussian CertGluePFL termination follows, but no completed milliscale four-label run is reported here. The causal estimand remains the same-law joint identified set, contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals, and sampled-data transfer remains fixed-compact or expanding-window rather than globally two-sided.
body.interpretation: For every encoded polyhedral-label Gaussian experiment, globally honest rules can now be replaced effectively by finite rational shared-trace rules with a computable vanishing coverage, risk, and ledger modulus; a final global full-set mixture restores exact honesty. Together with the already proved conditional termination theorem, this makes the Gaussian CertGluePFL procedure terminating. The multinomial experiment remains linked to this Gaussian target on fixed lawful compacts and on the declared expanding windows, not by a two-sided global unbounded transfer.
